newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Troubled Romanian bank to repay small depositors.
newsitem.headline: Troubled Romanian bank to repay small depositors.

text.p: Troubled Romanian private bank Dacia Felix SA, under court administration, will pay back up to a million lei to thousands of small investors staring on Wednesday, state news agency Rompres said.
It quoted Transylvanian court judge Ioan Geoargiu as saying the bank will unlock 235,000 accounts of small depositors and pay the interest due.
Dacia Felix, struggling with huge bad debts and heavy losses, was brought to its knees in mid-July by the withdrawal of central bank support.

The central bank asked a court in Dacia Felix's home town of Cluj to rule on its future, saying the troubled bank had stopped payments for more than 30 days. Dacia's banking license has not yet been withdrawn.
The court has granted Dacia time to reorganise or face liquidation. A meeting of shareholders is planned for next week.
Dacia has been in trouble for months after revealing over $200 million in bad debts and a 642.2-billion lei 1995 loss.
It owes creditors some 2.3 trillion lei and has to recoup 2.1 trillion from debtors.
The bank's major debtors are companies associated with its figurehead, former tennis player Sever Muresan, and the Grupul Darianne holding.
Muresan-led companies owed Dacia 1.17 trillion lei, of which 453 billion lei was interest repayments, while Darianne's debt amounted to 146 billion lei.
Geoargiu said individual deposits up to 10 million lei might be redeemed in the next three or four weeks. ($=3,176) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
